_comment: Copy this next to your Jarvis backend, edit it, and hand it to
jarvis_bots.app.build_supervisor. Dry-run it first with:
python3 -m jarvis_bots.app bots.config.json
which prints what it would build and, for everything it would not,
the reason in words. Nothing here is a default: a bot with no
section is not built, because a disk watch pointed at a guess is
worse than no disk watch.
Compares each card's PCIe link against the best ever seen for
that uuid, not against its theoretical maximum -- so a 170HX
sitting at Gen 2 x4 never alerts, and a card that *drops* from
its own best does.
Crash-loop detection fires even while systemd reports 'active',
which is exactly the case a plain up/down check misses: a unit
restarting every few seconds is active every time you look.
Two separate questions, two separate badge items: 'this is
nearly full now' and 'at this rate it fills on Thursday'.
The asset check is the one that catches a hosting rewrite
returning 200 and index.html for a bundle that is not there --
which looks perfectly healthy to a status-code check.
Off by default, and it stays off until you point 'fetcher' and
'parser' at your own code: this package ships no retailer's page
parser on purpose. The catalog that does ship names placeholder
shops at example.com, so the bot runs end to end without ever
touching a real site.
'windows' is the sniping half. Inside a window the poll interval
tightens to 'interval_s' (never under 30s -- that floor is in the
code, not here) and the bot's own tick rate follows it from ten
minutes before the window opens. That pre-arm is also when the
preflight runs: it checks there is a live push subscription, that
the source is not paused, that a rule can actually fire and that
the budget can afford it -- while there is still time to fix any
of them. A window where those are wrong raises an ACTION with the
reason, ten minutes early, instead of failing silently at 11:00.
It still does not check out. The alert carries a deep link to the
listing; you tap it and buy.
